page: Microsoft Azure D96as_v4 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the DASv4 family, powered by an AMD EPYC 7763 processor. Built on the x86_64 architecture, this instance features 96 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 48 physical cores with multithreading enabled. The processor operates at a clock speed of 3.525 GHz and is supported by 384.0 GB of system memory, yielding a balanced allocation of 4.0 GB of RAM per core. It includes 786 GB of local storage and is Premium Storage capable, running under the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor.

Benchmark data highlights strong multi-core performance, with stress-ng multi-core CPU testing placing the instance in the top 10% tier. Cryptographic capabilities are also highly rated, as evidenced by a top-tier score in the PassMark CPU encryption test. Memory performance is robust, with the PassMark memory score ranking in the top 10% and small-block cached read memory bandwidth reaching the top 25%. Multi-threaded decompression and database operations, including Redis SET operations, consistently register in the top 25% of tested hardware.

Given its high resource density and balanced CPU-to-memory ratio, the D96as_v4 offers qualitative cost efficiency for large-scale enterprise workloads that require substantial parallel processing without the premium cost of specialized memory-optimized or GPU-accelerated hardware. The absence of a dedicated GPU makes it less suitable for heavy deep learning training, though it maintains average to strong performance for small to medium LLM inference tasks. This configuration is highly suited for relational databases, multi-threaded data processing, software compilation, and high-throughput web serving.
